drivingQuestion: From where in Scripture are the mishna׳s restrictions on redeeming an ancestral field derived?
outcomeNote: The baraita answers מנא הני מילי for the clause ׳he may not borrow and redeem׳; the unit as packaged is a single segment and breaks off before the mishna׳s remaining clauses are derived.

segments.he: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר בְּרָחוֹק כּוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְהִשִּׂיגָה יָדוֹ״ — יַד עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִלְוֶה וְיִגְאַל.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: One «may not sell» his ancestral field that is located «in a distant» area and redeem with that money a field that he sold in a nearby area. Likewise, he may not sell a low-quality field and redeem with that money a high-quality field. And he may not borrow money and redeem the field, nor may he redeem the field incrementally, half now and half at a later date. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «As the Sages taught» with regard to the verse: “And he prospers and finds sufficient means to redeem it” (Leviticus 25:26), the phrase «“and he prospers”» teaches that the money he uses to redeem the field must be «his own possession,» meaning «that he may not borrow» money «and redeem» the field.
